title: The Instructions After the Appointment
title_ja: 診察の後に残された説明
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空例。実在の調査結果・医学的助言・法令・教授法の実証効果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional community health center provides visitors with a short written summary of the instructions discussed during their appointments.
sentences.ja: 架空の地域保健施設は診察中に話された指示の短い書面要約を来訪者に提供する。

sentences.en: The manager believes that distributing the document will make information more accessible and reduce the number of questions that visitors ask afterward.
sentences.ja: 文書配布が情報を利用しやすくし後で尋ねる質問の数を減らすと管理者は考える。

sentences.en: A staff member nevertheless wonders whether a document that appears clear to the people who prepare it will also be understandable to someone encountering the information for the first time.
sentences.ja: それでも作成者には明確な文書が初めて情報に接する人にも理解できるか職員は疑問に思う。

sentences.en: She proposes examining the communication process rather than assuming that the existence of a written summary demonstrates successful understanding.
sentences.ja: 書面要約の存在が理解成功を示すと想定せず意思疎通過程を調べることを提案する。

sentences.en: The center prepares several fictional examples of general administrative instructions, avoiding the use of actual patient information or medical treatment recommendations.
sentences.ja: 実患者情報や治療推奨を使わず一般的事務指示の架空例を用意する。

sentences.en: One example includes a request to bring a particular document to the reception desk before a future appointment.
sentences.ja: 一例は将来予約前に受付へ特定文書を持参する依頼を含む。

sentences.en: A visitor might recognize every word yet remain uncertain about which document is required, when it should be brought, or whom to contact if it is unavailable.
sentences.ja: 来訪者は全語を認識しても必要文書、持参時期、入手できない場合の連絡先が不明かもしれない。

sentences.en: The staff distinguish unfamiliar vocabulary from missing information about the action that the reader is expected to take.
sentences.ja: 未知語彙と読者がとるべき行動についての情報不足を区別する。

sentences.en: They consider revising the sample instructions to state the expected action more explicitly and to include a clear method for requesting clarification.
sentences.ja: 期待行動をより明示し追加説明を求める明確な方法を添えるよう見本を修正することを検討する。

sentences.en: The employees also discuss how a person could describe their understanding of a general instruction without feeling that they are being examined or blamed for a misunderstanding.
sentences.ja: 誤解で試験されたり責められたりすると感じず一般指示の理解を説明できる方法も議論する。

sentences.en: A brief conversation might reveal a difference between what a staff member intended to communicate and what the visitor understood the instruction to mean.
sentences.ja: 短い会話が職員の伝達意図と来訪者が指示の意味として理解したこととの違いを明らかにするかもしれない。

sentences.en: Such a difference can provide useful information for improving the explanation rather than simply identifying an error on the reader's part.
sentences.ja: 差は単に読者側の誤りを特定するのでなく説明改善の情報を提供し得る。

sentences.en: The manager recognizes that a shorter document is not necessarily easier to understand if the reduction removes details essential to completing a task.
sentences.ja: 短い文書でも短縮で作業完了に必要な詳細が消えれば理解しやすいとは限らないと認識する。

sentences.en: At the same time, including every potentially relevant detail in a single instruction could create unnecessary confusion.
sentences.ja: 同時に潜在関連詳細を全て一指示に含めると不要な混乱を生み得る。

sentences.en: The team considers separating essential actions from additional explanations that can be consulted when particular questions arise.
sentences.ja: 必須行動と特定の問いが生じたら参照できる追加説明を分けることを検討する。

sentences.en: This imaginary exercise does not establish the effectiveness of any actual clinical communication method or provide advice about medical care.
sentences.ja: 架空練習は実際の臨床意思疎通法の有効性を確定せず医療助言も提供しない。

sentences.en: Information becomes useful when the reader can understand how it relates to the circumstances in which a decision or action is required.
sentences.ja: 情報は判断や行動が必要となる事情にどう関連するか読者が理解できるとき有用になる。

sentences.en: The precision of a written statement is important, but the people who produce it may overlook assumptions that are unfamiliar to its intended audience.
sentences.ja: 書面の正確さは重要だが作成者は想定読者になじみのない前提を見落とすかもしれない。

sentences.en: Effective communication involves recognizing that the recipient may need additional information that the writer did not realize was missing.
sentences.ja: 効果的意思疎通は筆者が不足に気づかなかった追加情報を受け手が必要とする可能性の認識を伴う。

sentences.en: The fictional center therefore treats feedback about its instructions as a source of knowledge about the communication it is responsible for providing.
sentences.ja: そこで架空施設は指示への意見を提供責任を担う意思疎通についての知識源として扱う。

questions.prompt: What does the center provide after appointments?
options: A new diagnosis for every visitor.

questions.prompt: What concern does the staff member raise?
options: Visitors can never read any documents.
The instructions have never been prepared.
The document may seem clearer to its writers than to first-time readers.
questions.explanation_ja: 作成者と読者の理解差。

questions.prompt: What kind of examples are used?
Why may recognizing every word be insufficient?
options: Every familiar word is medically inaccurate.
A reader must memorize the writer's name.
The reader may still lack information about the required action.
The document contains no action at all.
Make every instruction longer without structure.
State actions explicitly and offer a way to request clarification.
Test all visitors on medical terminology.
Remove any way to ask questions.

questions.prompt: How can a conversation help improve instructions?
options: Reveal differences between intended and understood meaning.
Show that every visitor is mistaken.
Eliminate all need for written information.

questions.prompt: Why can shortening a document reduce its usefulness?
options: Short documents are always difficult to print.
All readers prefer the longest document.
General instructions and medical diagnoses exclusively.
Giving a written document guarantees understanding.
Communication should consider whether readers understand what to do, not just whether information is provided.
Any misunderstanding proves a reader's lack of effort.
questions.explanation_ja: 情報提供と理解の違い。

grammar.focus: whether a document that appears clear
grammar.explanation_ja: whether節がwondersの内容、that節がdocumentを修飾。

without feeling that they are being examined

paraphrases.source: A staff member nevertheless wonders whether a document that appears clear to the people who prepare it will also be understandable to someone encountering the information for the first time.
paraphrases.rewrite: A staff member questions whether readers understand a document as clearly as its writers do.

paraphrases.source: A visitor might recognize every word yet remain uncertain about which document is required, when it should be brought, or whom to contact if it is unavailable.
paraphrases.rewrite: Knowing the words does not necessarily tell a visitor what document to bring.

paraphrases.source: The employees also discuss how a person could describe their understanding of a general instruction without feeling that they are being examined or blamed for a misunderstanding.
paraphrases.rewrite: Visitors should be able to explain their understanding without feeling tested.

paraphrases.source: The manager recognizes that a shorter document is not necessarily easier to understand if the reduction removes details essential to completing a task.
paraphrases.rewrite: Shortening instructions can make them less clear if important details are removed.

discourse.role_ja: 意見を改善情報と捉える結論。
